name: Ras El Maa Spring
hero_subtitle: Where mountain water pours into town and everyday life gathers around it.

overview.title: The Spring That Made the Town Possible
overview.p1: Ras El Maa, literally 'head of the water', is a natural spring in the hills just outside the east gate of the medina. Cold mountain water rushes down a small stream through the old quarter, and for generations locals have used it for washing clothes and rugs.
overview.p2: It feels more like everyday life than a monument. Watch the stream, sit at a café by the water, or take the path that climbs from here towards the Spanish Mosque. Photograph respectfully: people are going about their day, so ask before you point a camera at someone.

1.title: The Spring and Stream
1.desc: See where the water comes out of the hills and follow the stream down towards the medina.

2.title: Riverside Tea
2.desc: A few small cafés sit right beside the stream. A calm place for tea and to listen to the water.

3.title: The Path Uphill
3.desc: From here a path climbs across the valley towards the Spanish Mosque viewpoint.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Ras El Maa Spring

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: It is a short walk from Place Outa el Hammam through the eastern alleys, downhill to the river. Follow the sound of water.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Mornings are quiet, late afternoons pleasant. After heavy rain the stream runs faster and louder.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: Please ask before photographing people, especially women washing clothes. Keep paths clear and mind wet stones.

q1.question: What does Ras El Maa mean?
q1.answer: Literally 'head of the water', named for the spring where the stream begins.

q2.question: How long do you need at Ras El Maa?
q2.answer: 30 to 60 minutes is enough for a walk, a look at the stream and a tea.

q3.question: Can you drink the spring water?
q3.answer: Locals use it for washing. If you are unsure, stick to bottled water.

q4.question: Is Ras El Maa free to visit?
q4.answer: Yes. It is an open, free area. You pay only for tea or food at the cafés.
